label: Epstein files / accountability
measure: Want more investigations and prosecutions in the Epstein case
question: Which side do you agree with more in relation to Jeffrey Epstein?
response: There should be more prosecutions and investigations into people associated with Jeffrey Epstein and his criminal activities
method: Global Strategy Group for Navigator; opt-in online panel, voter-file verified, demographic composition matched to the national registered-voter population. Methods also report additional interviews: 101 Hispanic, 99 African American, 75 Asian American/Pacific Islander and 100 independent voters.
uncertainty: Publisher reports ±3.1 percentage points at 95% confidence for the full sample. Opt-in panel; this reported margin does not capture selection bias or every source of survey error.
fit_note: Measures demand for further investigations and prosecutions, not guilt or willingness to protest. February 2026 opinion follows the 2025 events; coded Epstein demands are mostly about disclosure or cover-ups, not explicit prosecution. Historical context, not a matched opinion/action comparison.

label: Gaza / Palestinian solidarity
measure: Say Israel is going too far in its military operation against Hamas
question: Thinking about Israel’s current military operation against Hamas, is Israel…
rounding_note: Published rounded shares; totals may not sum to 100%.
method: American Trends Panel; national random sampling of residential addresses. Online or live-interviewer telephone. Weighted to US adults.
uncertainty: Full-sample sampling margin: ±1.9 percentage points (report methodology, printed p. 23). Wording, weighting and nonresponse can add error.
fit_note: A directional evaluation of military action, not support for every Palestinian-solidarity demand or protest. The 33% answering “not sure” remain in the denominator.

label: Racial justice / police accountability
measure: Strongly or somewhat support Black Lives Matter
question: From what you’ve read and heard, how do you feel about the Black Lives Matter movement?
rounding_note: Published rounded shares; totals may not sum to 100%.
method: American Trends Panel; national random sampling of residential addresses. Online or live-interviewer telephone. Weighted to US adults.
uncertainty: Full-sample sampling margin: ±1.6 percentage points at 95% confidence; not an item-specific interval. Other survey errors remain.
fit_note: Support for a named movement, not a measure of dissatisfaction. Black Lives Matter does not cover every racial-justice or police-accountability demand.

label: Abortion / reproductive rights
measure: Say abortion should be legal in all or most cases
question: Which comes closest to your opinion on abortion? Abortion should be...
response: Legal in all cases + Legal in most cases (published Legal NET)
rounding_note: Use the pollster’s published Legal NET of 64%. Separately rounded components are 25% and 38%, which sum to 63%; do not replace the published net with that sum.
method: Probability-based AmeriSpeak Omnibus; weighted to U.S. adults; age 18-29 oversampled. 1357 web and 80 telephone; English and Spanish.
uncertainty: Full-sample sampling margin: ±3.6 percentage points at 95% confidence; not an item-specific interval. Other survey errors remain.
fit_note: A legal-policy position, not dissatisfaction with existing laws or support for every reproductive-rights demand. Selected over pro-choice identity because it measures a concrete policy direction.
source_locator: Topline p. 15, ABO1; sample p. 1 and methods p. 23

label: Climate action
measure: Worry a great deal or a fair amount about climate change
question: I'm going to read you a list of environmental problems. As I read each one, please tell me if you personally worry about this problem a great deal, a fair amount, only a little, or not at all. First, how much do you personally worry about -- [RANDOM ORDER]?
method: Random-digit-dial telephone sample; minimum 80% cellphone and 20% landline respondents; weighted. Telephone; ReconMR fieldwork; Spanish interviews for primarily Spanish-speaking respondents.
uncertainty: Full-sample sampling margin: ±4 percentage points at 95% confidence; not an item-specific interval. Other survey errors remain.
fit_note: Concern is only an indirect proxy. It does not establish support for climate-action policies, the movement or its protests.

label: Immigrant rights / anti-deportation
measure: Oppose deporting all immigrants living in the US illegally
question: Would you favor, neither favor nor oppose, or oppose each of the following policies?
question_item: Deporting all immigrants living in the U.S. illegally
method: Probability-based AmeriSpeak Omnibus; weighted to U.S. adults; age 18-29 oversampled. 1357 web and 80 telephone; English and Spanish.
uncertainty: Full-sample sampling margin: ±3.6 percentage points at 95% confidence; not an item-specific interval. Other survey errors remain.
fit_note: Opposition to this blanket policy, not to every deportation. It does not cover all immigrant-rights demands; neutral responses are not counted as opposition.
source_locator: Topline p. 14, POLICIES2; sample p. 1 and methods p. 23

label: Ukraine solidarity
measure: Prefer US support for Ukraine reclaiming territory, even if war lasts longer
question: Which would you prefer the U.S. to do in the Russia-Ukraine conflict — try and end the conflict as quickly as possible, even if it means allowing Russia to keep territory it has captured from Ukraine (or) support Ukraine in reclaiming territory Russia has captured, even if it results in a more prolonged conflict between the two nations?
method: Random sample of probability-recruited Gallup Panel members; weighted to the U.S. adult population. Self-administered web survey.
uncertainty: Full-sample sampling margin: ±3 percentage points at 95% confidence; not an item-specific interval. Other survey errors remain.
fit_note: A conditional choice about US policy, not general sympathy for Ukraine or support for every solidarity protest. People preferring a quick end may still support Ukraine.
source_locator: Gallup-linked chart, August 2025; article Survey Methods
